title: [BUG] bone2d polygon assignment does not persist after edit
body:
### Tested versions

Noticed in 4.6.1 stable on debian.




### System information

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) x86_64

### Issue description

## issue
When assigning bones to polygons in the bone2d polygon editor the assignments do not persist, leading to incorrect bone structure. The user has no way to correct this issue making the skeleton2d feature unusable in 4.6.1.
Additionally, the design requiring a "sync bones" button to be manually pressed by the user each time they view this editor for each polygon is not desirable and could also lead to incorrect bone structure even if this bug were not present. 

## desired behavior
A fix should make it so the users assignment of polygon to bone persists even after the user moves focus on to a different edit menu. The users assignment should persist even if the user changes the skeletal structure—adding or removing unrelated bones. (ie. if the assigned bone has been deleted then it makes sense that its polygon assignment also should be deleted. however, if an unrelated bone has been deleted, it should not affect the polygon assignment for the other bones)
Additionally, a fix should reconsider the design of the editor in such a way as to not force the user to visit each polygon and manually sync the polygon to the skeleton.



### Steps to reproduce

## Steps to reproduce:
- create a tree of body part polygons a-la the tutorial (arms belong to torso node, head belongs to torso, forearm belongs to arms, etc...)
- move all nodes so it looks like the character is standing in a natural position
- edit the pivot points of each polygon so the pivot lies at the joint
- use the "make skeleton 2d" command to generate bones. This command will generate an incorrect skeleton structure (separate issue)
- fix the mess the "make skeleton 2d" command made by re-assigning the parentage of all bones so they resemble the hierarchy you originally built with the polygon nodes
- re-parent the whole tree to a skeleton2d node and set its rest position. There should now be no warnings in the scene tree.
- Select each polygon and assign the skeleton node to the skeleton property
- For each polygon, go to the bone2d editor in the bottom panel and "sync" the bones
- For each polygon, go to the bone2d editor and assign the correct bone for each polygon (arm polygon maps to arm bone, etc...)
- go back to the first polygon, notice how your edited bone assignment is now incorrect!
